sources.title: Economic Links and Predictable Returns
observed_method: Supplier–customer relations only used after a six-month fiscal-year-end gap; last available disclosed links, not present-day supplier maps.
Rank suppliers by previous-month equally weighted customer-stock return; five portfolios, rebalance monthly; long highest and short lowest for the studied spread.
sources.original_result_claim: Authors report about1.55pct monthly abnormal return for a long-short customer-momentum strategy. It is historical factor-adjusted spread evidence, not a verified net return for a500-dollar long-only account.
support_locations: Published journal pages1983(data timing),1985–1986(portfolio formation),1980(main summary).
sources.short_quote: we impose a 6-month gap between fiscal year-end dates and stock returns
sources.use_for_s500: Test whether publicly identified customer or industry-leader shocks help screen related suppliers; useful to expand beyond a fixed storage watchlist.
sources.new_hypothesis_not_original_rule: A500-dollar long-only single-position event strategy would be a new adaptation, not replication of the monthly diversified long-short paper.

sources.title: Do Industries Explain Momentum?
observed_method: Summary focuses on6–12month momentum horizons and industry component persistence.
Industry momentum may account for much individual-stock momentum in the historical study.
sources.use_for_s500: Industry strength is a possible conditioning variable, not a reason to buy any same-industry stock after an unrelated surge.
sources.new_hypothesis_not_original_rule: Adding a20-day sector filter to a3-day event trade is a separately registered hypothesis, not the6–12month paper.

sources.title: Standardized Unexpected Earnings
sources.published: 2019-09-10 page metadata; later2024 comment/update also visible
observed_method: Monthly top1000 by dollar volume with price>5 and fundamental availability.
Quarterly EPS difference versus four quarters before divided by standard deviation of prior seasonal EPS changes; tutorial uses36-month warmup and eight quarterly differences.
sources.claim_quality_issue: Page introduction cites Sharpe0.602 vsSPY0.43 for2009-12–2019-09; conclusion cites0.83 vs0.88. Version/backtest mismatch is unresolved, so no quantitative performance claim is adopted.
sources.use_for_s500: Provides an implementable earnings-surprise feature and a check against merely labelling a price jump as good news.
sources.new_hypothesis_not_original_rule: Choosing one affordable signal instead of a diversified top5pct basket materially changes the strategy. Use original as conceptual reference only.
missing_inputs: point-in-time EPS releases and restatement history
whole-share allocation and account execution costs
